title: steamed filipino savoy cabbage bao
description: a light and refreshing midnight craving dish that brings together the flavors of the philippines in a sattvic-friendly and easy-to-make bao. serve in a bento box for a delightful meal.
instructions: cut the savoy cabbage into small florets and set aside.
in a large mixing bowl, combine the glutinous rice flour and water to form a dough. knead the dough for 5-7 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
divide the dough into 4-6 equal portions, depending on how large you want your baos to be. shape each portion into a ball and then flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
heat a non-stick pan or ttukbaegi over medium heat and add the coconut oil. swirl the pan to coat the bottom evenly.
add the ginger and garlic to the pan and saut7 for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
add the soy sauce to the pan and stir to combine. bring the mixture to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes.
add the savoy cabbage to the pan and stir to combine. cook for 2-3 minutes until the cabbage is slightly tender.
place a portion of the cabbage mixture onto the center of each dough disk. fold the dough over the filling to form a bao shape and press the edges together to seal the bao.
place the baos on the bamboo skewers and steam in the ttukbaegi for 10-12 minutes until the dough is cooked through and the filling is tender.
serve the baos in a bento box with a sprinkle of sesame seeds on top.
